_readme: THIS APP'S DONE-RECORD — [pipeline N-2] Private/company/pipeline/06-app-build.md
Stamped with the app. It answers 'is this app done?' as a QUERY rather than a memory, and
tooling/ci/assert-app-dod.mjs fails the build on it. The right-hand side of every set comparison
below is tooling/dod-register.json — the DoD items, and the four human-review rows.
IT IS AN OUTPUT, NEVER AN INPUT. 39-CHASSIS §4 cut 4 stands: mason vars are the stamp's only
input contract. This file describes VERIFICATION STATE; it never feeds the stamp.
status:
stamped        a fresh stamp. Shape + the mechanical rows are enforced; the human verdicts and
the selection gates are recorded as pending, and their blanks do not fail.
claiming-done  everything is enforced. An app the public catalogue advertises as 'live' while
this still says 'stamped' FAILS THE BUILD — that cross-check is what stops
'stamped' becoming a permanent excuse.
features: the six the CHASSIS itself ships, so a freshly stamped app carries six REAL rows
rather than `features: []`. An app adds its own here as it builds them. Each row's `test` must
resolve to a real declaration with a non-empty body, `effect` must still name a symbol that is
there, and `mutation.date` EXPIRES: change the implementation and the row goes red until the
mutation is re-run and the date moved. That is the difference between an event and a state.
🔴 EVERY MUTATION BELOW WAS ACTUALLY RUN, on a real mason stamp, with `flutter test`, and the
named test was observed RED. Two candidate rows were REJECTED at that step rather than recorded:
a `themeMode` row whose mutation the suite did not notice, and an account-deletion row whose test
drives the seam in packages/auth_supabase rather than anything under this app — an effect anchor
outside the app cannot be re-dated against the app's own history. Account deletion is covered
instead by the chassis property `account-deletion-works`, which carries six anchors of its own.
A row whose mutation nobody watched is exactly the 'proven once in a terminal' claim this field
exists to replace.

A.note: the chassis ships the screen set; assert-screen-set.mjs holds the 22-screen register with anchors

B.note: human — the four-states verdict per data screen, recorded in humanReview

C.note: property ui-invariants-inherited pins the five Material window classes at 600/840/1200/1600 on the pure resolver AND pumps AppScaffold across the 600 boundary (rail at 768, bar at 375); responsive_width_test.dart measures the three ContentPane-capped screens at 375/768/1280(/1920)

D.note: properties theme-triplet-supplied + theme-mode-persisted, both limbs anchored (write AND read-back)

E.note: assert-no-hardcoded-strings.mjs; the chassis ships a second locale so the seam is really exercised

F.note: the mechanical WCAG limbs — text-scale clamp, 48px targets, non-empty icon labels

G.note: the stamp generates this app's OWN icons; assert-stamp-brand-assets.mjs compares against the live SDK's stock assets

H.note: the app_brick lane resolves, analyzes and tests this app on every push; the feature rows below carry the effect anchors

mutation.note: Re-run 2026-08-11 on a freshly stamped probe, because the awaited-sign-out change touched this same file and expired the row. Deleting the `await ref.read(authRepositoryProvider).updateProfile(displayName: displayName.trim())` call leaves the save button wired to nothing and the named test fails through its own expect at chassis_properties_test.dart:2079 — Expected: exactly one matching candidate / Actual: Found 0 widgets with text "Ada Lovelace", reason: 'the name was typed and saved and the screen still shows the old value — which is what a save button wired to nothing looks like'. `flutter analyze` reported "No issues found!" both before and under the mutation, so the red is an assertion and not a compile error; the file was restored byte-identical and the test re-observed green.
